title: Module semver guardrails and publish templates
content:
Overview:
This is a working note capturing a lightweight guardrail and publish template for Terraform modules used by Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal: reduce accidental breaking changes, make registry publishes repeatable, and provide an upgrade path for customers running pinned versions in private environments. This is intentionally pragmatic: a checklist + templates we can copy into PR descriptions and GitHub Actions.

Context and motivation:
- We've seen a few incidents where minor module changes required downstream manual fixes for on-prem customers (eg, provider schema changes, renamed outputs).
- Private customers often pin module versions tightly. We need clear versioning semantics, pre-publish compatibility checks, and a simple deprecation/upgrade communication flow.
- This doc is complementary to the TF module release checklist and onprem release playbooks; it focuses on versioning policy, compatibility testing patterns, and templates for registry publishing and deprecation notices.

High-level policy (proposal):
- Semantic versioning for modules: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
  - MAJOR: incompatible API change (output/variable renames, changes that break existing state).
  - MINOR: backward-compatible additions (new optional variables, additional outputs, new resources that don't require state migration).
  - PATCH: backward-compatible bug fixes and documentation changes only.
- No MAJOR version bump without a documented migration guide and >=2 review approvals (at least one from solutions engineering or SRE).
- Anything that touches resource addresses or state shape requires explicit migration testing and a canary release.

Pre-publish checks (automated + manual):
- Automated tests (must pass):
  - terraform validate (all supported TF versions)
  - terraform init + plan against a representative set of pinned examples (examples/compatibility/)
  - acceptance tests: run minimal apply/destroy in CI (cannot be flaky). Use lightweight providers/localstack where possible for CI.
  - cross-version plan checks: attempt a plan against the previous minor and previous major where relevant to detect drift.
- Diffed outputs/variables: run a script that diffs variable names and output names between tagged previous version and new branch. Fail if removals/renames are detected unless justified.
- Provider pinning policy: modules should not silently upgrade provider major versions. If bumping a provider major version, require MAJOR module bump or explicit compatibility shim.
- Manual review gates:
  - Any change flagged as "potentially breaking" by the diff script must include an RFC-style note in PR describing migration steps.
  - Solutions/SE or SRE must sign off on changes that alter resource addresses, names, or default behavior.

Compatibility-testing matrix (suggested):
- TF core versions: test against the earliest supported minor and latest patch of the current LTS range (e.g., 1.5.x and 1.8.x).
- Provider versions: test against currently supported provider minor versions where the module explicitly relies on provider features.
- Example stacks: run all examples under examples/ with the new module version and the immediate prior release. Keep a small set of customer-representative examples:
  - onprem-basic (VPC + static nodes)
  - onprem-k8s (VPC + k8s cluster bootstrap)
  - dedicated-proxy (gateway + TLS)

Registry publish steps (template):
- Branch name: release/module-<module-name>/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., release/module-priv-network/v1.2.3)
- PR template additions (copy into repo-level PR templates):
  - What changed (summary)
  - SemVer classification (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH)
  - Migration steps (if any)
  - Backwards compatibility testing performed (matrix) + CI links
  - Customer-impact checklist: list customers (internal label) pinned to previous versions if known

- GitHub Actions job: publish-to-registry (runs after CI passes + approvals)
  - Preconditions: tag vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH present + release branch merged to main
  - Steps: run `make release` (which runs tflint, tfsec, packer for artifacts), `terraform-docs` to update README variables/outputs, generate changelog if missing, bump module metadata, authenticate with registry (or private registry token), publish module, create GitHub Release with changelog.

Sample publish snippet (to include in repo docs):
- Tagging: git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "module: priv-network v1.2.3"
- Release: gh release create v1.2.3 --title "priv-network v1.2.3" --notes-file CHANGELOG.md
- Registry: (internal) curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TF_REGISTRY_TOKEN" 
  "https://registry.internal.redwood/api/modules/publish?module=priv-network&version=1.2.3"

Breaking-change checklist (must be completed for MAJOR changes):
- [ ] Migration guide (documented, example code for new state migration)
- [ ] Deprecation window defined (recommended: at least 90 days for private deployments)
- [ ] Automated migration test in CI (simulate upgrade path on example infra)
- [ ] Customer impact list and outreach plan (CS/Solutions owns comms)
- [ ] Rollback playbook (exact commands to restore prior module version + state restore steps)
- [ ] Approval from security/compliance if any change affects secret handling, network defaults, or audit logging

Deprecation notice template (for release notes / customer email):
Subject: Deprecation notice — module priv-network v1.x => v2.0.0 scheduled
Hello —
We plan to publish priv-network v2.0.0 on <date>. This release contains incompatible state changes and requires a migration. We recommend customers pinned to v1.x to test the migration guide prior to the scheduled date. Outline:
- Why: reason for break (brief)
- Impact: what will break if users do nothing
- Migration steps: high-level + link to migration doc
- Support: contact customer-success@redwood.ai or open PD ticket PCC-<id> for assist

Rollout strategy for private deployments:
- Canary: publish to registry, mark as "canary" and push for non-production customers who opt-in (label in support portal)
- Staged releases: after 2 weeks of canary validation, open for general availability for new installs only; after 60 days, recommend for upgrades.
- Emergency rollback: publish patch on v1 branch if a regression is found and push alert to SRE + notify customers.

Automated tooling we should add (TODOs):
- "tf-module-diff" script: given two tags, prints variable/output/resource additions/removals and classifies as breaking/non-breaking. (Prototype exists in tools/ but needs hardening.)
- Registry publish GitHub Action that integrates with our internal registry API, attaches migration guide, and tags module as canary/ga.
- Customer pinning dashboard: a simple query into usage metrics that maps customers to pinned module versions (helps prioritization).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Deprecation window length: 90 days is a balance but enterprise customers may need longer. Should be configurable per module.
- Force-major vs compatibility-shim: sometimes we can add a shim variable to preserve old default behavior and avoid MAJOR bump; trade-off is technical debt. Use MAJOR if shim complexity is high.
- Where to record migration scripts for state transformations? Keep in examples/migrations/v2_to_v3/ and mention in changelog.

Quick snippets and helpers (copy into .github/):
- PR labeler: add `semver:major|semver:minor|semver:patch` label mandatory for release PRs.
- Small bash helper to detect output/var removals (naive):
  git fetch origin main && git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep "variables.tf\|outputs.tf" && ./scripts/tf-diff-vars-outputs.sh origin/main HEAD

Notes to self / next actions:
- Clean up tools/tf-module-diff and add tests (owner: Diego)
- Draft GitHub Action for publish-to-registry (owner: Asha)
- Run a trial release for priv-network module to validate the flow (target: April sprint)
- Sync with CS on customer pinning visibility and plan outreach cadence

References and related docs:
- internal Confluence: Private Deployments - Module Lifecycle (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- existing checklists: onprem-tf-module-release-checklist-draft.json (see sibling file)

---
This doc is purposely conversational and task-oriented — intended to be copied into repo READMEs and PR templates. Feedback welcome.
